source: APPP / MAFF-JICA — Rice Seed Production Manual (សៀវភៅមគ្គទេសក៍ផលិតកម្មពូជស្រូវ), 2014, Agricultural Productivity Promotion Project in West Tonle Sap, p.9
text: To select only healthy, well-filled seed before sowing, producers use a salt-water flotation method: (1) Weigh out 20 kg of salt. (2) Dissolve the salt into a container holding about 40 liters of water. (3) Stir thoroughly until the salt is fully dissolved. (4) Test the solution's concentration by dropping in an egg or a sample of unhusked seed — if the egg/seed floats appropriately at the surface, the salt concentration is correct. An alternative recipe using ammonium sulfate is also given: about 8 kg of ammonium sulfate dissolved in 40 liters of water. Seed grains are then poured into this brine; grains that float (empty, poorly filled, or diseased) are skimmed off and discarded, while grains that sink to the bottom are the healthy, well-filled seed to be kept for sowing. The solution should be prepared fresh and kept away from contamination by chickens or cattle.
